definition: A detailed description of what something must do or contain.
business_context_example: Build to the specification, not to what you think the client meant.

definition: A detailed technical drawing or plan.
business_context_example: The blueprint shows two exits, but only one was built.

definition: A technical diagram of a part or structure.
business_context_example: Check the latest drawing, revision C, not revision B.

definition: The allowed difference from an exact measurement.
business_context_example: The tolerance is plus or minus 0.2 millimetres.

definition: A measurement such as length, width or height.
business_context_example: One dimension on the drawing was in inches, and that cost us a week.

definition: An early working model built to test a design.
business_context_example: The prototype worked; the production version didn't.

definition: An investigation into whether a plan is practical.
business_context_example: The feasibility study said the site was too small.

definition: Supporting weight in a structure.
business_context_example: That wall is load-bearing, so it stays where it is.

definition: One part of a larger machine or system.
business_context_example: A single component failed and stopped the whole line.

definition: Putting parts together; also the finished group of parts.
business_context_example: Final assembly takes 40 minutes per unit.

definition: A quantity produced at one time.
business_context_example: The whole batch was rejected because of one bad weld.

definition: The percentage of production that meets quality standards.
business_context_example: Yield improved from 91% to 97% after the new fixture.

definition: The amount of work or material passing through a system.
business_context_example: Throughput doubled, but so did the queue at packing.

definition: The point in a process that slows everything else down.
business_context_example: The bottleneck is the single paint booth, not the machines.

definition: To increase production or capacity.
business_context_example: Scaling up from 100 to 1,000 units needs a second shift.

definition: The time between ordering something and receiving it.
business_context_example: Lead time on that valve is 14 weeks, so order now.

definition: To adjust an instrument so its measurements are accurate.
business_context_example: We calibrate the sensors every six months.

definition: To test and start up new equipment so it is ready to use.
business_context_example: The line was commissioned in April and ran from May.

definition: To take equipment permanently out of service.
business_context_example: The old boiler will be decommissioned next winter.

definition: Time when a machine or system is not working.
business_context_example: Unplanned downtime costs us about 900 euro an hour.

definition: A problem that stops something working correctly.
business_context_example: The fault was in the wiring, not the motor.

definition: A flaw that makes a product fail to meet standards.
business_context_example: Two defects per thousand units is our current rate.

definition: To find and fix the cause of a problem.
business_context_example: He troubleshot the line remotely and saved a site visit.

definition: The real underlying reason a problem happened.
business_context_example: The root cause was a loose bracket, not operator error.

definition: Normal damage from regular use over time.
business_context_example: Fair wear and tear is expected; this was misuse.

definition: Planned servicing done before something breaks.
business_context_example: Preventive maintenance every 500 hours has cut breakdowns by half.

definition: A thorough repair or rebuild of a machine.
business_context_example: The compressor is due for a full overhaul in August.

definition: To add new parts or technology to older equipment.
business_context_example: We retrofitted the old presses with new controls.

definition: Damage to metal caused by chemical reaction, such as rust.
business_context_example: Corrosion around the joints means water is getting in.

definition: Weakening of material after repeated stress.
business_context_example: The crack was metal fatigue after years of vibration.

definition: A test that pushes something to its limits to see when it fails.
business_context_example: The stress test ran for 72 hours at double the normal load.

definition: Able to last a long time without damage.
business_context_example: The coating is more durable but twice the price.

definition: Checking that products meet the required standard.
business_context_example: Quality control caught it before the shipment left.

definition: An official rule about how something must be made or done.
business_context_example: The part meets the ISO standard, so the audit was easy.

definition: To formally approve work as complete and correct.
business_context_example: The site engineer signs off on every stage before the next starts.

definition: The formal transfer of a finished project to the client.
business_context_example: Handover is on the 12th, with all documentation.

definition: A list of small items to fix before a project is accepted.
business_context_example: The punch list has 23 items, mostly paint and sealant.

definition: Drawings showing how something was actually constructed.
business_context_example: Send the as-built drawings, not the original design.

definition: A trip to the place where work is being done.
business_context_example: One site visit answered questions three emails couldn't.

definition: A company or person hired to do a specific job.
business_context_example: The main contractor is responsible for all the trades on site.

definition: A company hired by the main contractor to do part of the work.
business_context_example: The electrical work went to a subcontractor from Sofia.

definition: A study of what could go wrong and how to prevent it.
business_context_example: No risk assessment, no work. That's the rule on this site.

definition: Something that could cause harm.
business_context_example: Report any hazard, even if you fixed it yourself.

definition: Personal protective equipment, like helmets, gloves and goggles.
business_context_example: PPE is mandatory beyond this line, no exceptions.

definition: Locking a machine off so it can't start during maintenance.
business_context_example: Lockout before you open the guard, every single time.

definition: An incident that could have caused injury but didn't.
business_context_example: We log every near miss, because the next one might not miss.

definition: To stop a machine or system completely.
business_context_example: Shut the line down before you clear the jam.

definition: To make a copy of data in case the original is lost.
business_context_example: Back up the controller settings before the update.

definition: To decide that something is not the cause.
business_context_example: We ruled out the software, so it's mechanical.

definition: To find a way past a problem without solving it fully.
business_context_example: We worked around the faulty sensor until the new one arrived.
